title: Fourier weight and approximation near π/2
statement: There exists a real constant $C\ge0$ such that, for every natural number $n$, every $\{-1,1\}$-valued function $f$ on $\{0,1\}^n$, and every real $\varepsilon\ge0$ for which $|\widehat f(\{i\})|\le\varepsilon$ for all coordinates $i$, the level-one Fourier weight satisfies $W_1[f]\le 2/\pi+C\varepsilon$. Moreover, if $2/\pi-\varepsilon\le W_1[f]$, then $f$ disagrees with the threshold sign of its degree-one Fourier part on at most a fraction $C\sqrt{\varepsilon}$ of the uniformly chosen cube points.
hypotheses_covered: there exists a real constant C
every singleton Fourier coefficient has absolute value at most ε
the lower-bound premise 2/π − ε ≤ W₁[f] for the approximation conclusion
replaced:
For $n\in\mathbb N$ and a real-valued function $f$ on $\{0,1\}^n$, use uniform expectation $\mathbb E[h]=2^{-n}\sum_xh(x)$, singleton Fourier coefficients $\widehat f(\{i\})=\mathbb E[f(x)(-1)^{x_i}]$, degree-one Fourier weight $W^1[f]=\sum_{i<n}\widehat f(\{i\})^2$, and degree-one part $L_f(x)=\sum_{i<n}\widehat f(\{i\})(-1)^{x_i}$; define $\tau(r)=1$ for $r\ge0$ and $\tau(r)=-1$ for $r<0$.
There exists a real constant $C\ge0$ such that, for every $n\in\mathbb N$, every sign-valued function $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$, and every real $\varepsilon\ge0$ with $|\widehat f(\{i\})|\le\varepsilon$ for every $i<n$, one has
\[
W^1[f]\le\frac2\pi+C\varepsilon
\quad\text{and}\quad
\left(
\frac2\pi-\varepsilon\le W^1[f]
\ \Longrightarrow\
\Pr[f(x)\ne\tau(L_f(x))]\le C\sqrt\varepsilon
\right),
\]
where the probability is uniform on the cube.
